subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram provider intermittently stalls despite stable direct Bot API connectivity

question: Should Telegram SOCKS failures be fixed through a shared scheme-aware proxy transport contract now, and should that repair be based on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/84582 or a replacement PR?
rationale: The source path is plausible, but the remaining choice affects shared proxy semantics and the open candidate PR is partial and unproven, so automation should not open another fix PR or close the issue without maintainer direction.

options.title: Require shared proxy repair plus live proof
options.body: Keep this issue open and require a focused repair that covers explicit and env proxy schemes, preserves HTTP proxy defaults, and includes redacted live Telegram or equivalent proxy proof.

options.title: Accept explicit-only PR scope
options.body: Maintainers could choose to land only the explicit proxy change and track env proxy coverage separately, accepting the remaining compatibility risk.

options.title: Wait for fresh reporter repro
options.body: Maintainers could defer code changes until a current-main SOCKS5 service-context reproduction is posted, leaving the open PR paused.

recommendation.title: Require shared proxy repair plus live proof
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require a focused repair that covers explicit and env proxy schemes, preserves HTTP proxy defaults, and includes redacted live Telegram or equivalent proxy proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest routing signal is the shared proxy helper merge history plus later review ownership around proxy compatibility-sensitive changes.
